pr_title: Include the exception when logging in WebAssemblyErrorBoundaryLogger

issue_context.title: Using Custom ILogger with ErrorBoundary produces exception = null
issue_context.body:
I have a blazor webassembly project with a custom ILogger that worked fine. However, after I used the new ErrorBoundary, the public void Log method of the ILogger is called with logLever = Error and a null exception. ```razor @Body
Error:@ex.Message
Reload refresh
```
comments: Thank you for filing this issue. In order for us to investigate this issue, please provide a minimalistic repro project (ideally a GitHub repo) that illustrates the problem.

Hi @musamalou. We have added the "Needs: Author Feedback" label to this issue, which indicates that we have an open question for you before we can take further action. This issue will be closed automatically in 7 days if we do not hear back from you by then - please feel free to re-open it if you come back to this issue after that time.

To reproduce the issue follow these steps:
 1. Place a break point in the log method of the CustomLogger.cs.
 2. Run the project
 3. Click on Counter/Error menu
 4. Clikc on the 'Click Me' button to throw an exception
 6. Check the value of the exception.
 7. Run the project without enclosing @Body in ErrorBoundary

**The Result is: Without an error boundary, you should get the exception in log method of CustomLogger.cs that was thrown from the counter.razor** 

8. Now enclose the @Body in ErrorBoundary and build and run the project again

 The Result is: With the body enclose in the ErrorBoundary tag, the error is thrown, but the exception in the log method of CustomLogger.cs is null
[BlazorAppWithILoggerErrorBoundary.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/files/7736579/BlazorAppWithILoggerErrorBoundary.zip)

review_comments: I think this is wrong, as the `exception` comes before the `message`. See #39223
